text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced back 2.45% today after dropping nearly 9.5% over the past two weeks, as oil markets stabilized on mixed signals about Middle East tensions. US crude held at $99.64 a barrel while Brent briefly dipped below $90 earlier in the week on hopes of de-escalation—Trump suggested an Iran conflict could end "fairly soon"—but Secretary of State Rubio countered that diplomatic talks remain stalled, creating uncertainty about whether oil prices will stay depressed or spike again. For a refiner like Marathon, lower crude prices cut into profit margins (the "crack spread," or the difference between what they pay for oil and what they earn selling refined products), so the week's oil price swoon weighed heavily; today's rebound suggests some relief as traders price in the possibility that geopolitical risk won't evaporate as quickly as Trump implied.

Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity with ample fuel inventories on hand, so demand isn't pulling prices higher—the recovery is mostly a shift in how much geopolitical premium investors are willing to pay. The uncertainty itself has made the stock volatile; any concrete news on Iran could swing it sharply either direction again.
